summary: John's 4th-great-grandfather; a coal miner at Mardyke in the Slieveardagh coalfield of Tipperary who died in Ireland before his widow and sons emigrated.
bio: Thomas Heffernan was baptized at Gortnahoe on 10 Sep 1808, son of Humphrey Heffernan, 'a miner living at Lickfin', and Anastasia Ryan. He married Catherine Boney at Gortnahoe on 3 Feb 1833 and lived at Mardyke, where he was a miner (Dwyer, Branch 4). Mardyke and Lickfinn were collieries in the Slieveardagh coalfield; the Mining Company of Ireland opened its Mardyke mine in 1824 with a Cornish engine and 25 workers' cottages. His children were Jude (bapt. 14 Jul 1839), Andrew Humphrey (bapt. 3 Apr 1842), Richard (bapt. 22 Dec 1844), Catherine (bapt. 6 Feb 1848) and John (bapt. 29 Aug 1852). He died in Ireland, probably between 1852 and about 1864; his son Andrew's obituary mentions only 'his mother and brothers' coming to America. His brother Richard married Catherine's (possible) sister Anastasia Boney; his brothers James and Patrick were transported to New South Wales after the 1834 Ballynonty killing. TREE CORRECTION: Johnny's tree shows Andrew's father as 'Thomas Heffernan 1791-Deceased' (with an obituary-clipping image), son of Patrick Heffernan (1763-1871) and Catherine Neagle (1770). In Dwyer the Thomas baptized in 1791 is Thomas 'of Lanespark' (Branch 1), son of Patrick and Catherine Neagle, who married Catherine Shelly in 1831 - a different man. Dwyer found no proven link between the Patrick/Neagle family and the Humphrey/Ryan family.
